summary: Setting up an Asana OAuth app is a moderate task requiring registration in the developer console and implementation of the authorization code grant flow. While private apps are easy to create, publishing to the App Directory requires a formal submission and review process.

approval.notes: Approval is required if you intend to publish your app to the Asana App Directory; private apps do not require review.

steps.title: Register the application
steps.detail: Navigate to the developer console to create a new app and obtain your client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Configure OAuth settings
steps.detail: In the OAuth tab, set your redirect URL and select the required permission scopes for your application.

steps.title: Implement OAuth flow
steps.detail: Build your server to handle the authorization code grant flow, including the user authorization endpoint and token exchange.

nuances: Native or command-line apps should use the special redirect URL 'urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob'.
Non-native apps must use HTTPS for redirect URLs.
Client secrets must never be exposed in source code.
Asana does not support making token requests directly from a browser.
agent_can_do: Draft the app name and description for the developer console.
Configure redirect URLs and select necessary scopes based on app requirements.
Store client ID and secret in secure environment variables.
Verify the OAuth flow implementation against Asana's documented endpoints.
human_must_do: Sign in to the Asana developer console.
Submit the app for review if publishing to the App Directory.

create_app.quote: You must first register your application with Asana to receive a client ID and client secret.

credentials.quote: Once you have created an app, the OAuth tab in the sidebar will include a client ID (needed to uniquely identify your app to the Asana API) as well as a client secret .

redirect_uri.quote: Redirect URL - Otherwise known as the callback URL , this is where the user will be redirected upon successful or failed authentication.

approval.quote: Set your distribution to “any workspace”, then follow the instructions on the Developer Console > Submit for Review page.
